extracted.intended_audience: Applicants and peer reviewers for the CIHR Project Grant Program (Canadian health researchers, administrators, and knowledge users)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandates for preparing and submitting applications to the CIHR Project Grant competition and for peer reviewers assigning/assessing those applications. Includes peer review committee mandates, resubmission rules, CV requirements, equity/assessment guidance, and Priority Announcement rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee selection at registration
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying for funding, at the time of registration, you should suggest up to two committees whose mandates most closely align with your research project. Suggested committees must remain unchanged between registration and application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your application overlaps with more than one area of science, select the peer review committees that best reflect the research area and objectives. CIHR will consult with committee Chairs and Scientific Officers and will make the final decision on which peer review committee will review each application based on the summary of proposed research received during registration. The final committee selected may not necessarily be your first or second choice. The final list of committees held for a given competition may differ from the list available at registration. Applicants will be informed which committee reviewed their application on Notices of Recommendation and Decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioural Sciences – A (BSA) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic studies, employing non-human models, in which the primary goal of the study is to establish the neurobiological basis of behaviour. Focus on neurobiological mechanisms of motivation, emotion, stress, drug abuse, feeding, reproduction, learning/memory, pain, motor function and circadian rhythms. Animal models of neurological/psychiatric disease and behavioural recovery from stroke/injury are appropriate when endpoints are primarily behavioural.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods include Pavlovian/associative conditioning, instrumental/operant conditioning (including self-administration), behavioural tests, pharmacological or genetic manipulations, neurophysiology, molecular biology, biochemical assays — provided behavioural endpoints are central.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioural Sciences – B: Clinical Behavioural Sciences (BSB) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical and clinically relevant studies in at-risk or human psychiatric, neuropsychiatric, and neurological populations where expected outcomes have direct clinical relevance (risk, diagnosis, treatment, survival/mortality, remission quality, adverse events).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodologies include observational, interventional, longitudinal, cross-sectional studies focusing on phenotyping, psychosocial determinants, sleep studies, risk modeling, imaging, genetic/epigenetic analyses, biomarkers, electrophysiology, and interventions. Note: studies whose primary aim is mechanisms of cognition, learning, memory, sensory/motor functions, perception, attention, sleep, pain, speech/language, neuro control of gait should be sent to BSC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioural Sciences – C: Behavioural Studies, Neuroscience and Cognition (BSC) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanistic studies using cognitive, systems, or behavioural neuroscience approaches (in humans or animals) to study mechanisms of cognition, learning, memory, sensory and motor functions/integration, perception, attention, sleep, pain, speech/language, neuro control of gait.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable methods include behavioural testing, psychophysics, electrophysiology, brain stimulation, structural/functional neuroimaging, molecular/cellular techniques, neuroanatomy, eye tracking, pain imaging, computational neuroscience, and large-scale network dynamics. Clinical/applied psychiatric studies should go to Behavioural Sciences B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology – A (BMA) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Structural, chemical, and biophysical studies of biomacromolecules and their interactions, including structural characterization, biophysical techniques (X-ray, EM/cryo-EM, NMR, mass spectrometry, spectroscopy), computational approaches, enzyme mechanisms, protein engineering, structure-guided drug discovery, chemical biology, and analysis of biomolecular variation/mutation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Studies with a primary focus on proteins/nucleic acids other than structural studies should be referred to Biochemistry & Molecular Biology – B (BMB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biochemistry & Molecular Biology – B (BMB) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies on molecular mechanisms of biological systems focusing on nucleic acid and protein function (chromatin, chromosomes, organelles; DNA/RNA metabolic processes; replication, recombination, repair, transcription, processing, splicing, transport, translation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Structural focus should go to BMA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological and Clinical Aspects of Aging (BCA) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Cellular and molecular mechanisms of aging, cell senescence, stress response, longevity/premature aging genes, animal models of aging, predictive markers of biological health, molecular/cellular basis of age-related tissue changes, causes/prevention/treatment of geriatric syndromes (falls, frailty, delirium), management of chronic pain, and cognitive decline in the elderly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biomedical Engineering (BME) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Engineering and development of biomechanical, medical, and molecular devices including prosthetics, artificial organs, nanosystems; numerical models of physiological systems; biomaterials; biomechanics; regenerative medicine, tissue engineering, repair/regeneration; organ/tissue preservation; molecular and nanoscale technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: gait studies, biomechanical movement studies, and rehabilitation-focused studies should be referred to Movement & Exercise (MOV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancer Biology & Therapeutics (CBT) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Carcinogenesis; basic and translational aspects of vaccine, metabolism and gene therapy; radiation biology; experimental radiotherapy; cancer immunotherapy; cancer prevention approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancer Progression & Therapeutics (CPT) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Cancer progression biomarkers, tumor microenvironment, development of innovative pharmacological agents/targets, molecular targeting therapies, exploratory translational cancer research with focus on pre-clinical studies, molecular epidemiology of tumor markers, and methods for early detection, prevention and management of cancer-associated morbidities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cardiovascular System – A: Cells and Tissues (CSA) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Research on cellular, molecular and genetic mechanisms of cardiac diseases, from gene/cell/tissue development to genetic animal models; studies on gene transcription, mitochondrial/cell biology, cell metabolism, signal transduction, ion channels; methods include genetic manipulation, cardiac tissue engineering, electrophysiology, imaging, nuclear pathway analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cardiovascular System – B: Heart and Circulation (CSB) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Research on heart and circulation: hemodynamics, hypertension, myocardial protection, cardiac remodeling, ischemia/reperfusion, neuro- and endocrine regulation; animal models, genetic models, pharmacogenomics, gene discovery and expression studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Clinical studies should be referred to Clinical Investigation – D: Cardiovascular Systems (CID).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cardiovascular System – C: Vascular System (CSC) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Research on the vascular system including endothelium; cellular, molecular and immune mechanisms regulating cardiovascular function in health/disease; atherosclerosis, inflammation, thrombosis, and vascular homeostasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell Biology – Molecular/Fundamental (CB1) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Molecular cell biological mechanisms governing basic cell function: junctions, endocytosis, secretion, protein sorting/traffic/degradation, cytoskeleton, organelle biogenesis/dynamics, cell-matrix mechanisms, cell cycle, cell-cell communication, signal transduction, development, protein folding, phase-separation, quality control, cell death, pattern formation, differentiation, morphogenesis; using primarily cell models from multicellular organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Developmental mechanisms using embryonic/iPSC/3D organoids should be referred to CBC or CBB or relevant organ panels; structural biology to BMA; gene regulation/transcription to BMB; obesity studies to DOL; spinal cord injury/repair to Neurosciences (NSA, NSB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell Biology – Disease (CBB) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations examining cell biology mechanisms underpinning acquired diseases and/or developmental origins of disease; disease processes impacting cellular phenotypes rooted in mutant/aberrantly expressed proteins; model cells, disease models, iPS models, primary cultures, relevant human tissues/cells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: structural biology to BMA; gene regulation/transcription to BMB; obesity to DOL; spinal cord injury/repair to Neurosciences panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell and Developmental Physiology (CBC) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations relating cell biology to cell physiology and systems networks: structure/function, membrane bioenergetics, organelle dynamics, lipid–protein interactions, ion channels, model systems (organoids, yeast, Drosophila, C. elegans) that inform cell physiological/biological responses and mechanisms in health/disease; systems biology of development; computational/quantitative cell biology; gene expression and differentiation during development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: skeletal muscle contraction studies -> MOV; cardiac muscle studies -> CSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Investigation – A (CIA) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical and clinically-relevant translational studies on reproductive, maternal, fetal, neonatal, infant, child and youth health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: social/developmental aspects of children's and youth's health should be referred to Social & Developmental Aspects of Children's & Youth's Health (CHI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Investigation – B (CIB) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical and clinically-relevant translational studies in arthritis, bone, cartilage, oral health and dermatology, including developmental processes of these tissues, joint diseases, dental diseases, rheumatology, orthopaedics, bone/mineral metabolism, oral/craniofacial structures, and wound healing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Investigation – C (CIC) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical and mechanistic human studies in metabolic and endocrine disorders; gastroenterology, hepatology, nephrology, urology, hematology and related viral/microbial pathologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Only non-malignant hematology applications accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Investigation – D: Cardiovascular Systems (CID) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical studies on heart and circulation: hemodynamics, hypertension, myocardial protection, remodeling, ischemia/reperfusion, cardiovascular clinical pathophysiology, diagnosis and therapeutics, arterial/venous vascular disease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization (CMZ) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects where a product/process/service to be commercialized has been identified; IP and IP protection strategy identified and described; IP subjected to an initial technology assessment. Research to determine commercial viability, strengthen IP value, improve business prospects or downstream investment, and promote academic-industry collaboration to accelerate commercialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications to this committee should include a Research and Technical Plan and a Commercialization Plan as part of the research proposal. Applications solely focused on prototype construction will not be considered. Existing licences/options do not disqualify. Discipline-based committees are appropriate for projects intended to help academic and industry collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diabetes, Obesity, Lipid & Lipoprotein Disorders (DOL) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Molecular, cellular and whole organism studies of carbohydrate, protein, lipid and energy metabolism related to fundamental and translational biology of diabetes, obesity, metabolic syndrome and dyslipidemia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: population/human nutritional studies should be referred to Nutrition, Food & Health (NUT). Immunology of type 1 diabetes -> Immunology (IMN).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender, Sex & Health (GSH) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: How sex (biological) influences mechanisms of disease, health and behaviour and how gender-related (psychosocial) factors influence health status, outcomes, behaviours and health-services use; emphasizes intersectional life-span approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must address sex and/or gender influences in all aspects of the application (significance, hypotheses, methods, model/target population, measurement tools, recruitment, power calculations, analytic strategies, interpretive challenges). Single-sex/gender studies may be considered but must include clearly-articulated rationale. Studies on reproductive/maternal health should go to Clinical Investigation – A (CIA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genetics (G) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Inherited diseases and susceptibility, mutation mechanisms, modeling human genetic diseases, genotypes/phenotypes/natural history, metabolic genetics, population/statistical genetics, cytogenetics, epigenetic inheritance, gene regulation, DNA repair/replication/recombination, gene and gene-based therapies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genomics: Systems and computational biology (GMX) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical or conceptual advances in genome research related to high-throughput methodologies (proteomics, epigenomics, metabolomics, transcriptomics, metagenomics, pharmacogenomics/nutrigenomics), conceptual/technical advances in molecular and cellular systems-level analysis, high-throughput synthetic biology approaches, bioinformatics, computational algorithms and software development supporting these areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: research focused mainly on biochemical/molecular methods not addressing genomic/systems approaches may be beyond GMX mandate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health Policy & Systems Management Research (HPM) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Health policy and politics, health economics, health systems management, health human resources, learning health systems adaptation/change, and related system-level research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: primary focus on children/youth, elderly, or gender issues should be referred to CHI, SDA, or GSH respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health Services Evaluation & Interventions Research (HS1) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Health care interventions and programs including those engaging health professionals or other care providers designed to improve organization, use and delivery of services; research that examines outcomes (health status, quality, effectiveness, efficiency, accessibility, costs, equity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes innovative methods/tools for studying services; relates to any sector, level of care, condition, population, or delivery mode. Education/training related to general competency/distribution of health professionals -> HPM. Adaptation/implementation/fidelity/uptake studies -> Knowledge Translation Research (KTR). Child/youth development studies -> CHI. Older adults -> SDA. Gender-primary studies -> GSH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hematology, Digestive Disease & Kidney (HDK) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies of mechanisms of disease including cellular physiology and molecular biology with emphasis on translational research in hematology, gastroenterology/hepatology, nephrology, and urology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects related to malignancies, chemotherapeutic drug mechanisms and transplantation DO NOT fall within this committee. Clinical/mechanistic human studies should be referred to Clinical Investigation – C (CIC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanities, Social Sciences, Law & Ethics in Health (HLE) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Health research from humanities (history, philosophy, law, literary and cultural studies, narrative analysis, arts-based research, communication/media analysis) or social sciences (health studies, sociology, anthropology, political science); includes health ethics and health law; research may be critical, theoretical, methodological or empirical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: primary focus on health services/evaluation -> HS1; determinants of health -> PB1; health policy emphasis -> HPM; population/public health -> PH1; child/youth health -> CHI; elderly -> SDA; gender issues -> GSH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immunology (IMN) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Research into innate/adaptive immunity and immune function at genetic, molecular, cellular, model organism, whole animal or human levels; immune cell development/differentiation, host-environment interactions (including microbiota), immune-stromal interactions, immune reconstitution/homeostasis/tolerance, inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases, immunity to infection with focus on immune mechanism, immune cell transformation and immunotherapies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: transplantation surgery focus -> relevant discipline-based committee; organ preservation for transplantation -> BME. Microbial pathogenesis/viral immunization focused on pathogen -> MID or VVP. Host-response-focused using pathogen as tool -> IMN. Investigations of immunotherapies where focus is development/optimization rather than in-depth immune function -> CBT, MID, or VVP as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indigenous Health Research (IHR) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews applications with central focus on ethical and culturally informed research involving Indigenous peoples, promoting health through research aligned with Indigenous values/traditions and following TCPS 2 Chapter 9 guidelines; includes all four research pillars and interdisciplinary approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on deep community engagement, partnership, collaboration, integration of service to community within scientific excellence, research responding to Indigenous priorities, capacity-building, use of a range of disciplinary and community-based methodologies, and adherence to TCPS 2 Chapter 9 and local Indigenous partnering ethical guidelines. Applicants must indicate how project addresses TCPS 2 Chapter 9 and Indigenous partnering/organizational guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge Translation Research (KTR) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge Translation and Implementation Science research evaluating theory, interventions, and/or implementation processes aimed at fidelity, adaptation, implementation, scale-up and/or sustainability of evidence-based interventions, procedures or policies; assessing indicators/impacts of KT interventions or implementation processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: systematic review applications should be referred to the relevant discipline-based committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical Physics & Imaging (MPI) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Development and optimization of medical imaging technologies (MRI, x-ray, CT, ultrasound, nuclear, molecular and optical imaging) with validation/application in pre-clinical models or clinical populations; basic imaging science; radiation therapy and biophysics technology development; computational/experimental methods and translation; technical advancements can include software and/or hardware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: studies using off-the-shelf methods without technical innovation are best suited to relevant systems/disease committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microbiology & Infectious Diseases (MID) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Molecular and cellular microbiology and physiology emphasizing (non-viral) bacterial, fungal and parasitic pathogens; microbiome contributions to health/disease; host-pathogen interactions; vaccine discovery/development; antimicrobial mechanisms/resistance; molecular diagnosis and new therapeutics development; pathogen-focused mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Virology -> VVP; host response-focused immunology -> IMN. RCTs lacking basic science components should be directed to RC1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Molecular & Cellular Biology of Cancer (MCC) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental molecular, cellular and genetic mechanisms of cancer etiology including discovery research on tumorigenic processes: cell signaling, cell cycle/proliferation, stromal–tumor interactions, angiogenesis, carcinogenesis, stem cell fate/differentiation, epigenetics, growth regulation, apoptosis, metastasis; DNA repair and related translational aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Movement & Exercise (MOV) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Gait studies, biomechanics, skeletal muscle biology, fiber typing and regulation, skeletal muscle contraction, movement disorders, neuromuscular disorders, myopathies, sensory motor integration, exercise physiology, role of exercise in health/rehabilitation, rehabilitation and physical therapy, orthopaedics, occupational ergonomics, kinesiology, health and physical fitness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: cardiac muscle-related studies -> CSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systems & Circuits Neurosciences (NSA) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems neuroscience and analysis of circuitry underlying behaviour, network dynamics and changes in circuit function; includes cellular/molecular mechanisms of neurodegenerative, neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders, axonal regeneration, neural circuit repair, neuronal death/degeneration, protein misfolding, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial deficits, vascular pathology, endogenous neurogenesis, stem cell biology for repair; motor/sensory/homeostatic systems and related disorders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approaches include animal models, molecular/cellular approaches, gene transfer/therapy, drugs/pharmacology, imaging, functional assays (electrophysiology, behaviour). Note: basic behavioural endpoint research -> Behavioural Neuroscience A (BSA); human/clinical psychiatric/neurological studies -> BSB or other clinical committee; large-scale network dynamics/computational neuroscience -> BSC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Molecular & Cellular Neurosciences (NSB) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Molecular and cellular neuroscience: neurobiology, neurotransmitters/signaling molecules, cellular/molecular mechanisms of neurological disorders, axonal/dendritic development, synaptogenesis, activity-dependent development, ligand/voltage-gated ion channels, G-protein linked receptors, neurotransmitter release, synaptic transmission, synaptic plasticity, neuronal excitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: network dynamics/system neuroscience/sensory systems -> NSA. Skeletal muscle/myopathies/exercise -> MOV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nutrition, Food & Health (NUT) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding role of nutrition in health/disease through basic research and animal models, nutritional epidemiology, intervention studies including RCTs; topics include impact of food/nutrient intake and eating behaviours on health, mechanistic studies on nutrient metabolism, pathogenesis of nutrient imbalance, human nutrition across life span, energy balance, health consequences of diets/supplements, dietary assessment methods, food intolerance/allergy, nutrition-related education/health promotion, socioeconomic/cultural/political influences on nutrition, non-oral feeding strategies, precision/personalized nutrition, nutrigenetics/nutrigenomics/metabolomics, and machine learning approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pharmaceutical Sciences (PS) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Drug design and delivery including medicinal chemistry, radiopharmaceuticals, biopharmaceutics, drug analyses, pharmacokinetics, drug discovery from natural compounds, and xenobiotics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pharmacology & Toxicology (PT) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications on uses, effects and modes of action of drugs and compounds: methodology of drug action, drug metabolism and toxicology, drug abuse/addiction, characterization of drug targets, pharmacology of biological substances, clinical pharmacology, pharmacogenetics, pharmacodynamics, xenobiotics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychosocial, Sociocultural & Behavioural Determinants of Health (PB1) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioural and social sciences research applied to physical and mental health, health behaviour, psychophysiology, community health and well-being across the life course including palliative/end-of-life care; focuses on behavioural, psychological, social, cultural, environmental and contextual perspectives related to health promotion, prevention, mechanisms, disease processes, outcomes, treatment, and intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include psychometric measurement, knowledge synthesis, behavioural medicine, clinically applied projects or efficacy trials. Emphasizes conceptual models, theory testing, a priori hypotheses, well-justified design, rigorous measurement and sound analyses. Quantitative/qualitative/mixed methods and various designs are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public, Community & Population Health (PH1) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Conception and measurement of exposures and health status and testing hypotheses concerning exposure/disease relationships: epidemiologic studies from gene/environment interactions to social environment impacts, research on etiology of disease/disability, population health intervention research, development/application of statistical methods, burden of disease measurement, global health, health inequalities, diverse and disadvantaged populations, health promotion, water safety and impact of global change on health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: child/youth development -> CHI; older adults -> SDA; gender-primary studies -> GSH; nutrition/food safety -> NUT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomized Controlled Trials (RC1) mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies where investigators randomly assign eligible human participants or other human units (classrooms, clinics, etc.) into groups to receive or not receive interventions; includes pilot/feasibility RCTs and studies using novel RCT designs, and studies on development of methodologies for design/conduct of randomized clinical trials. RC1 is multidisciplinary across CIHR's mandate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respiratory System (RS) mandate (partial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research on the lung and associated tissue from cellular and animal models to clinical research with respiratory endpoints or sequelae; neural control of breathing, lung development and mechanics, lung transplant, diseases including restrictive and obstructive lung diseases, cystic fibrosis, respiratory diseases of adults and newborns, sleep-related breathing disorders, acute lung injury and lung inflammation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmissions: definition and allowed responses
rubrics_metrics.description: What is a resubmitted application? Applicants may provide a response to previous reviews when resubmitting; if providing a response they must attach all the reviews and Scientific Officer (SO) notes (if provided) they received related to reviews they are responding to. If a response is included without attaching the relevant previous reviews and SO notes, the response will be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may choose to respond only to comments relevant to their revised application. When referring to comments from a particular competition, all reviews and SO notes of that competition MUST be attached. Previous reviewer comments may only stem from previous Project Grant competitions (not other funding opportunities). Example scenarios clarify attachment expectations for second, third submissions and which past reviews must be attached. Response to previous reviews has a 2-page limit (2.5 pages in French) for third resubmissions context noted in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for attaching previous reviews and SO notes
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant provides a response to previous reviews they must attach all the reviews and Scientific Officer notes (if provided) they received related to the reviews to which they are responding. If not attached, the response will be removed from the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When addressing comments from multiple past competitions, applicants must attach reviews and SO notes from each of those competitions. Previous reviewer comments may only come from previous Project Grant competitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant CV requirements (CCV vs Applicant Profile)
rubrics_metrics.description: All Canadian academic applicants, regardless of role on application, must submit a Biosketch CV completed through the Canadian Common CV (CCV). Knowledge users, non-academics, Indigenous organizations, or international applicants may submit either a Biosketch CV or a streamlined Applicant Profile CV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant Profile CV may not exceed three pages and has no section restrictions — applicants choose what to emphasize. Collaborators are not required to provide a CV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer accounting for sex- and gender-based analysis (SGBA)
rubrics_metrics.description: In evaluating applications, peer reviewers assess whether sex- and gender-based analysis (SGBA) is a strength, weakness, or not applicable; this assessment should be reflected within their written evaluation and the overall score assigned to the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: DORA and research assessment guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR is a signatory of DORA and directs reviewers not to use journal-based metrics as surrogate measures of individual research publication quality. Reviewers are encouraged to consider a range of research outputs beyond journal articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can highlight diverse contributions and impacts (publications, reports, books, guidelines, datasets, code, tools, training/mentorship, volunteerism, community engagement, standards, software, commercialized products) and impacts (policy/practice influence, health/societal outcomes, culturally safe Indigenous research). Reviewers should consider context affecting applicant productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equalization policy for specified groups
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR will ensure the proportion of grants funded for Early Career Researchers (ECRs), female NPIs, applicants submitting in French, NPIs self-identifying as racialized, and NPIs self-identifying as a person with a disability is at least equal to the proportion of applications submitted by those groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If highly ranked applications from these groups are not funded at levels at least equal to application rates, CIHR intervenes by funding additional applicants based on their percent rank. For more information see Project Grant Program: Results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual peer review model: core aspects retained
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtual peer review mimics the in-person face-to-face process; CIHR has retained all core aspects but made adjustments for technology and online meeting format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Virtual model can improve work-life balance, reduce carbon footprint, and enable participation of individuals who could not attend face-to-face meetings, increasing diversity and inclusion and allowing more international reviewers. CIHR is evaluating the virtual process and community feedback will inform future approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Announcements (PAs): purpose and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority Announcements are additional sources of potential funding for highly ranked Project Grant applications relevant to CIHR Institutes, Initiatives and Partners. Three types: One-year grant / Multi-year grant (top-down funding below competition cutoff), Supplemental Funding ('Top-up') to encourage inclusion of specific approaches in funded applications, and Prizes/Awards allocated to highest ranked funded applications relevant to a specific area/career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can identify up to three PAs for consideration. Each PA includes a description of target research area; some PAs require a short relevance form (~half-page) while others use the application summary to assess relevance. Applicants must consent to sharing information to be considered for PAs; not consenting makes them ineligible for PAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Announcement relevance and selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevance of applications to a PA is assessed separately by the CIHR Institute/Initiative/Partner (using relevance forms and/or application summary) and is not part of the peer review process. The peer review does not assess PA relevance and relevance has no impact on peer review deliberations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions of Institute/Initiative/Partner regarding relevance are final and not open to appeal. Applicants are encouraged to provide a compelling and factual case in the relevance form or clearly demonstrate relevance in the summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Announcement funding eligibility rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications rated below 3.5 are not eligible for PA funding. For one-year/multi-year PAs, applications below the competition funding cut-off but relevant to a PA may be funded top-down until PA funds exhausted. Supplemental funding will be allocated to highest-ranking funded Project Grant applications relevant to selected PAs. Prizes/Awards allocated to highest-ranking funded applications relevant to a Prize PA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is funded through Project Grant peer review, full funding comes from the Project Grant budget (unless PA is supplemental/top-up or prize). If application is top-ranked on two PA lists, only one PA will be awarded. PA grants are not counted in the Project Grant competition success rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to share information for PA consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must consent to the sharing of information in order to be considered for Priority Announcements. Applicants who do not consent will be considered ineligible for PAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance forms for some PAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Priority Announcements require applicants to complete a relevance form (~half-page free form text) to describe how and why their application is relevant to the PA area. For PAs not requiring a relevance form, relevance is assessed using the application's summary of research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The relevance form and/or summary will be considered by the Institute/Initiative/Partner or Partner funding the PA.

rubrics_metrics.name: What happens if application deemed relevant and also funded in Project Grant
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is deemed relevant to a PA and is successful in the Project Grant competition, additional funds are received only if the PA is supplemental funding or a Prize. For other PA types the application will be funded via the Project Grant budget and PA funds will be used to support the next highly ranked application below the cut-off.
